auditor_check.evidence: Ran the regex taken verbatim from build-manifest.mjs line 257 (/^##\s+(?:[A-Z]\d+\b|No findings)/im) over 11 seat-file shapes: empty and header-only files are missing, and a level-three heading is missing; a file cut off right after a claim heading, one cut inside an open Evidence fence, one whose only claim heading sits in a code fence, a lower-case claim heading, '## No findings yet, still working', and a hypothesis-tag heading all count as a complete seat, so initBody marks the run completed and build-report prints COMPLETE with two passes.

evidence: Shipped initBody over 11 seat-file shapes: cut-off, fenced, lower-case and prefix shapes read completed.
Shipped initBody plus validateProblems: six malformed shapes read completed while failing validation.
findings.summary: The new Phase 1 seat-file gate accepts any file holding one claim-like heading, so a cut-off, fenced-only or malformed seat file still yields a completed manifest and a COMPLETE report.
findings.recommended_fix: In build-manifest.mjs initBody (line 257), decide completeness with the existing fence-aware, role-specific seat-file validation (validateProblems) instead of the raw heading regex, or at least require an unfenced '## Checks performed' or exact '## No findings' heading; add tests for a file cut off after a claim heading and a fenced-only heading.

auditor_check.evidence: claude-dispatch.mjs: the timeout callback on an exited child without an answer sets stream.timedOut and resolves with no kill and no stopIncomplete; the stopIncomplete warning block runs only when stoppedAfterAnswer is set; line 532 then reports 'claude -p killed after exceeding --timeout' although nothing was signalled. With no timer (review-run.mjs line 421 passes --timeout 0 by default) only child.on('close') resolves the run, and close waits for any process still holding stdout or stderr, so the step never ends. The physical orphan run was not repeated by me.

evidence: Fake claude CLI with no result event and a detached child holding the output: --timeout 0 never ends (result.json stays running); --timeout 4 records timed-out 'killed' with no stopIncomplete.
findings.summary: A seat CLI that exits without a successful answer while a child it started holds its output hangs the dispatcher forever under the default --timeout 0, and under a finite timeout is recorded as killed with no stopIncomplete warning.
findings.recommended_fix: In runClaude and runCodex, on child exit without a successful answer start the same bounded close wait the answered path uses, then resolve with the exit code, stopIncomplete true and the 'output still open' warning; at claude-dispatch.mjs line 532 (and the codex equivalent) say 'timed out' rather than 'killed' when the child had already exited.

auditor_check.evidence: Imported shipped scrubDir and runDirNamedIn and used an existing folder under the home folder as the run folder: 'C:\Users\...\<tail>', the Unicode-ellipsis form, 'C:\Users\<user>\<tail>', 'C:\Users\%USERNAME%\<tail>', 'C:\Users\$env:USERNAME\<tail>' and the bare tail with either separator all gave scrub 0 and guard pass; controls (absolute path rewritten, ~ and %USERPROFILE% blocked) behaved as designed. %USERNAME% expands to the real user name on this host, so that spelling is fully resolvable.

evidence: Shipped scrub then guard: ellipsis, placeholder, %USERNAME%, $env:USERNAME and tail spellings all pass unrewritten.
findings.summary: The run-folder guard after the rewrite lets abbreviated, user-name-variable and root-less tail spellings of the run folder reach the peer view and the auditor.
findings.recommended_fix: In path-utils.mjs expandPathVars expand %USERNAME%/$env:USERNAME/${USER}; in build-brief.mjs runDirNamedIn also refuse text holding the run folder's last two or three segments joined by any separator (case folded where foldsCase says so), which only refuses and so errs safe.

auditor_check.evidence: Shipped scrubDir then runDirNamedIn over 11 backticked sibling shapes: suffixes '2', '-evidence', '.bak' pass untouched; '+1', '@x', '(2)', 'é', '中' and '.é' are left unrewritten by the scrub but refused by the guard (mentionsDir only treats [A-Za-z0-9._-] as a name continuation); a quoted ' 2' sibling is still rewritten to '<run-dir> 2'; a run path glued to CJK prose is no longer rewritten and is refused. Statically, build-recheck-packet.mjs rewritePaths treats '.' followed by a non-ASCII letter as a path end, so a '.é' sibling is rewritten. One over-broad origin bundles the recheck rewrite and the quoted-space rewrite with the scrub/guard boundary mismatch; all share the fix of one shared folder-name boundary.

evidence: Shipped scrub then guard: '+', '@', '(' and CJK-glued paths are left by the scrub and refused by the guard.
Shipped scrubDir, runDirNamedIn and rewritePaths over twelve siblings: refusals, a quoted-space rewrite and a recheck rewrite of Unicode dot-suffix siblings.
findings.summary: The scrub, the run-folder guard and the recheck path rewrite disagree on where a folder name ends, so sibling folders are refused as the run folder, still rewritten when space-continued, or rewritten in recheck packets.
findings.recommended_fix: Define one folder-name boundary in path-utils.mjs and use it in scrubDir, build-brief.mjs mentionsDir and build-recheck-packet.mjs rewritePaths (continuation set [\p{L}\p{N}_+@(.-], dot followed by a Unicode letter or digit is a continuation); the residual space-sibling rewrite in the scrub is a documented trade-off only for unquoted paths.

evidence: Shipped seatBlockedLine over 25 shapes: letter, roman, number-dash, definition-colon, em-dash and full-width-colon blocks after a none return empty.
findings.summary: After an earlier 'Blocked: none', a block behind a letter or roman list marker, a dash-like marker, a definition colon or a full-width colon is not read, so a blocked No findings seat passes as clean.
findings.recommended_fix: In review-run.mjs LOOSE_BLOCKED_RE (line 774), accept any run of non-letter, non-digit characters plus an optional short letter, roman or number label before 'blocked', and a full-width colon.

auditor_check.evidence: Shipped agentState and agentLastReply on Claude-style transcripts: earlier turn replies 'written', a new user prompt follows, and the last turn ends with empty content, thinking only, or blank text: state done and reply is still the earlier 'written'; a new text reply is read correctly. review-run.mjs lines 241-243 therefore add no warning.

evidence: Shipped agentLastReply: three empty-last-turn Claude transcripts keep the earlier 'written'.
Shipped agentLastReply over eleven transcript shapes: five native empty-turn shapes keep 'written'; the task-event shape returns null.
findings.summary: For a resumed native Claude agent, a turn that ends with no text inherits the previous turn's 'written', so the new no-reply warning never fires.
findings.recommended_fix: In native-agent.mjs agentLastReply (lines 125-135), set reply to null on each user entry that isNewPrompt marks as a new prompt, as claudeState does.

auditor_check.evidence: Shipped scrubDir then runDirNamedIn with the target as base: 'plugins/../../../cross-review-runs/closing-r4/<run>/file' and its backslash form gave scrub 0 and guard pass, while the './..' and '../..' controls were blocked; pathStartRe's win32 branch never starts a path at a directory name, so such a token is never resolved.
auditor_check.severity_reason: The leak is real but needs a seat to write a target-relative path that walks out through '..' into the run folder (pre-flight keeps the run folder outside the target), which seats rarely do, and peer seats already know the run folder from their scratch path.

evidence: Shipped runDirNamedIn, scrubDir and build: ten directory-led relative variants accepted by both builders; './' and '../' controls refused.
findings.summary: A run-folder path written relative to the target and starting with a directory name (dir/../../<runs>/...) passes both the rewrite and the guard into the peer view, the auditor and the briefs.
findings.recommended_fix: In build-brief.mjs runDirNamedIn, also resolve tokens of the form <name>[\/]...[\/]..[\/]... (any path token holding a '..' segment) against the target before the existence check; add those variants to tests/build-brief.test.mjs.

auditor_check.evidence: Shipped seatBlockedLine on '## No findings / Blocked: none' followed by a Checks performed heading holding 'Blocked: target: EACCES': plain, '1.'-numbered, level-three and differently cased headings return the block, but bold, italic, underscore, double-underscore, code-marked and '(1)'-numbered headings return '' because SEAT_SECTION_RE does not match them and the level-two heading ends the No findings section, so the gate passes the seat.

evidence: Shipped review-run phase1 --wait on a bold Checks performed heading after a none: code 0, 'validate Phase 1: clean'; six of eleven heading variants passed.
findings.summary: A Checks performed heading wrapped in emphasis or code marks, or numbered '(1)', is not recognised, so a block declared under it after an earlier 'Blocked: none' leaves a blocked No findings seat passing as clean.
findings.recommended_fix: In review-run.mjs seatBlockedLine, strip emphasis and code marks and a '(N)' or 'N.'/'N)' number from the heading text before testing SEAT_SECTION_RE (line 773); add those heading variants to the completion-gate tests.

auditor_check.evidence: preflight.mjs stopOnSignal (lines 550-562) calls killTree on the child with no hasExited check, and cross-review opencode-dispatch.mjs installSignalForwarding (lines 73-86) and its timeout callback (lines 534-550) call killTree likewise, unlike the guarded claude and codex dispatchers; on win32 killTree runs taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F on the stored pid. An actual reused-pid kill was not shown.
auditor_check.severity_reason: The missing exited-child guard is real, but a wrong kill needs a stop signal or timeout in the window after exit while output stays open plus pid reuse, which was not shown; the previous round rated this exact shape in the other dispatchers MEDIUM.

evidence: Shipped runWithTimeout with an injected exited child: ten exited-state variants each requested taskkill /pid /T /F; opencode signal helper requested kills for all eight exited states.
findings.summary: Preflight's signal handler and the OpenCode dispatcher's signal and timeout paths still tree-kill the pid of a child that already exited, the sibling of the guard added to the other two dispatchers.
findings.recommended_fix: Apply the hasExited(child) guard from spawn-utils.mjs before killTree in preflight.mjs stopOnSignal and in opencode-dispatch.mjs installSignalForwarding and its timeout callback; add exited-child tests for each.
